headline: Venture firm Andreessen Horowitz says its new ranking of consumer AI apps shows few people paying for the main chatbots and the top 10% of spenders supplying about half of the spending it tracked.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a detailed industry ranking with new spending data, but it is one investor's analysis of US panel data rather than a news event.
importance_line: Shows that few people pay for the main AI chatbots and that heavy users supply much of the spending, with a16z saying reaching everyone else will likely take different products and perhaps ads or transaction fees, but the spending figures are US-only panel estimates, not company revenue, from a firm that invests in the field.
summary: Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), a venture capital firm that invests in AI, published the seventh edition of its Top 100 Gen AI Consumer Apps list, which for the first time adds a ranking by observed spending on US consumer cards, using panel data from the data firm YipitData. a16z reports that only 4.5% of US consumers in that panel paid for at least one of ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude in August, that the top 10% of spenders account for roughly half of observed spending, and that ChatGPT still leads with about three times as many US paying subscribers as Claude or Gemini, with Claude now a clear third.
notes: Read in full on a16z.com (HTTP 200); published 6 Oct 2026 02:38 UTC per the pool. a16z's own analysis of third-party panel data (YipitData, Similarweb, Sensor Tower); its notice says some information comes from third parties, including its portfolio companies. The short descriptions of a16z and YipitData are ours (general knowledge and the article's 'investing team'). Kept MOD per default_v1; could also sit in MKT.
